claims.text: Precisely narrowing the precursor reduction-and-nucleation window prevents excessive adatom diffusion in noble metal–based high-entropy alloy nanoparticle syntheses.
Preventing excessive adatom diffusion suppresses phase separation and elemental segregation.
A broadly controlled reduction-and-nucleation window permits enough atomic mobility to cause inhomogeneous alloy formation.
Sufficient atomic mobility causes uncontrolled nanoparticle morphology.
The relevant starting material is a well-mixed, finely dispersed mixture of noble- and base-metal salts or elemental precursors.
Adjusting a kinetic parameter such as heating ramp rate can systematically narrow the temporal window for reduction and nucleation while other conditions remain fixed.
The proposed mechanism operates under rapid, high-temperature, nonequilibrium synthesis conditions.
Pulsed laser deposition is a scalable and cost-effective fast-heating implementation of the proposed synthesis conditions.
The balance between precursor reduction or nucleation rate and subsequent adatom mobility governs alloy uniformity.
Rapid reduction and nucleation cause nuclei to form before adatoms can diffuse significantly.
Limited adatom mobility preserves near-equilibrium nanoscale mixing.
Pronounced atomic diffusion drives high-temperature phase separation in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
Broadening the reduction-and-nucleation window causes excessive diffusion and uncontrolled morphology.
Narrowing the reduction-and-nucleation window will significantly improve alloy homogeneity relative to an unchanged baseline.
Narrowing the reduction-and-nucleation window will significantly improve morphological control relative to an unchanged baseline.
Leaving the kinetic parameter unaltered produces a broader temporal window, greater adatom diffusion, more phase segregation, and less controlled morphology.
The hypothesis applies particularly to systems containing more than five interacting elements.
The hypothesis does not apply to long-duration thermal treatments dominated by equilibrium diffusion.
The optimal temporal window and required kinetic adjustment are unspecified and may depend on precursor chemistry and experimental setup.
Failure of the modulated run to show a statistically significant improvement in homogeneity or morphology over the otherwise identical baseline would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The synthesis is described as nonequilibrium and kinetically dominated, yet limited diffusion is said to preserve 'near-equilibrium mixing.' Near-equilibrium mixing would ordinarily require sufficient equilibration or diffusion, so this phrase conflicts with the proposed diffusion-limited mechanism.

The intervention assumes a precursor-reduction window, whereas the cited pulsed-laser-deposition route alternately deposits pure metals and does not establish a salt-reduction step whose duration can be narrowed by a heating ramp.
